relations: Hand holds lever steady, keeping nozzle height and discharge orientation nearly unchanged.
Viscous liquid emerging from nozzle tip forms a thin vertical thread.
Flow-rate changes make tip beads swell and the strand thicken, narrow, then stretch downward.
A falling drop-like mass remains connected to the nozzle as it moves out of view.
caption: The video captures a close-up of a white plastic pump dispenser, its ribbed collar and threaded shaft visible beneath a lever nozzle that a hand grips from above with thumb and forefinger. A viscous, translucent-white liquid is already emerging from the nozzle tip, hanging as a thin vertical thread against the blurred pale basin behind. The hand holds the pump steady while the stream evolves. A rounded bead swells at the tip and the flow thickens into a wobbling strand that falls out of view. Partway through, the strand bulges again at the nozzle before stretching downward once more. This heavier flow then narrows, while a drop-like mass moves downward out of view, leaving a long thin thread. As the view continues, the discharge settles back into a thin, mostly steady vertical thread with minor thickness wobbles. Throughout, the lever and the gripping fingers remain at nearly the same height, and the liquid continues to flow from the nozzle.
